rules.statement: Don't change the signature (parameters, return type or nullability) of a shipped public method; add a new overload instead.
rules.why: Shipped public surface is a contract consumers depend on, so it evolves only additively after GA, and changing a signature is a breaking change.
rules.check: Look in the diff for edited public method signatures and matching edits to PublicAPI.Shipped.txt, or *REMOVED* lines for shipped members, where an overload could have been added instead.

rules.statement: Add a new optional input to a public type as a nullable `init` property that the library defaults when null (failing closed), never as a new constructor parameter.
rules.why: A new constructor parameter changes the binary signature and breaks every `new T(...)` call site and serializer. Resolving the default inside the library keeps the default out of consumer code.
rules.check: Look for a public constructor that gains a parameter, especially an optional one, and for new optional properties that aren't nullable or that leave consumers to supply the default.

rules.statement: Make a public configuration callback take a single growable options type (`Action<TOptions>`), and add new settings as properties on that type, not as new callback parameters.
rules.why: An options type grows by adding properties, but adding a bare callback parameter breaks every caller.
rules.check: Look for public methods that take delegates with several configuration parameters, or diffs that add a parameter to an existing configuration callback.

rules.statement: Append new members to a public or serialized enum and never reorder or renumber existing members.
rules.why: Reordering or renumbering changes the serialized wire values.
rules.check: Look for enum diffs that insert members in the middle, reorder them or change explicit values of existing members.

rules.statement: Remove shipped public surface only in a major version, after it has been marked `[Obsolete("…", error: false)]` and kept working in an earlier minor release.
rules.why: Deprecating first, then removing across a major gives consumers time to migrate without a break in a minor or patch release.
rules.check: Look for deleted public types or members (or *REMOVED* lines for shipped API) that weren't previously marked [Obsolete], or that are removed without a major version bump.

rules.statement: Don't share one public type across two packages that version independently; keep it in a single owning package or duplicate it deliberately.
rules.why: A type shared by packages that can version apart causes a diamond dependency conflict.
rules.check: Look for a public type moved into, or referenced as part of the public surface of, two independently versioned packages.

rules.statement: Treat a nullability change on a public signature (`string` ↔ `string?`) as a tracked, potentially breaking API change.
rules.why: Nullability is part of the signature, and the `#nullable enable` header in the PublicAPI files records it.
rules.check: Look for public parameters, return types or properties whose nullable annotation changes, and check that the change is intended and versioned accordingly.

rules.statement: Record new public API in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, and mark removed API with a `*REMOVED*` prefix there instead of deleting lines from `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt`.
rules.why: PublicApiAnalyzers compares the compiled surface against both files. The Unshipped diff makes surface changes visible and intentional in the PR.
rules.check: Check that a PR changing public surface includes an intentional PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt diff, that Shipped.txt is edited only at release, and that removals use *REMOVED* lines.

rules.statement: Bump the major version whenever shipped public surface is removed or an existing signature changes.
rules.why: Once GA, only additive changes are allowed in minor and patch releases.
rules.check: If the diff removes public API or alters a shipped signature, check that the package version is bumped to a new major.

rules.statement: In PublicAPI.*.txt files, write interfaces without variance annotations (`IFoo<T>`, not `IFoo<in T>`), and don't list compiler-synthesized record members.
rules.why: The analyzer doesn't match annotated or synthesized entries, so they cause RS0016/RS0017 build errors.
rules.check: Look for `in`/`out` in generic interface entries and for synthesized record members (Equals, GetHashCode, ToString, Deconstruct, PrintMembers, operators) listed in the files.

rules.statement: In PublicAPI.*.txt files, don't list a `Type.Type() -> void` constructor for a non-positional `record class`, but do list it for a non-positional `readonly record struct`, and list the `Ns.Class.extension(Receiver!)` block marker line for C# extension members.
rules.why: The analyzer excludes the implicit parameterless constructor of a record class but includes it for a record struct, and it requires the extension block marker. Getting either wrong raises RS0016/RS0017.
rules.check: Look for constructor lines on record classes, missing constructor lines on record structs, and extension members that have no block marker line.
